subject.title: fix: parse provider rate-limit reset timestamps for smarter cooldowns

question: Should OpenClaw accept free-form provider reset timestamp parsing as default auth-profile cooldown behavior, or require a typed reset-hint/quota contract first?
rationale: The PR can make existing profiles unavailable for much longer based on provider message parsing, which is an auth-provider compatibility and product-policy choice rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Typed reset-hint contract first
options.body: Require the PR or replacement work to carry validated reset metadata through all prompt and assistant failure paths before changing default cooldown behavior.

options.title: Accept broad parsing as default
options.body: Allow the free-form parser approach, but only after explicit maintainer acceptance, focused coverage, and real-run proof.

options.title: Defer to quota circuit-breaker work
options.body: Pause this branch if maintainers prefer to settle periodic quota classification and long-disable semantics in the overlapping circuit-breaker lane first.

recommendation.title: Typed reset-hint contract first
recommendation.body: Require the PR or replacement work to carry validated reset metadata through all prompt and assistant failure paths before changing default cooldown behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent short-window rate-limit retry work is the closest current owner signal for deciding how reset windows should interact with assistant failover and retry policy.
